stories.title: World's second-largest Bitcoin mining hub cuts power to rigs in its capital
stories.summary: CoinDesk reports that miners in the country with the world's second-largest Bitcoin mining capacity are shutting down rigs in its capital city amid strain on the mining sector. Separately, CryptoSlate flags a roughly $48 billion cluster of leveraged Bitcoin futures positions that could trigger mass forced liquidations if price breaks key boundaries.
stories.whyItMatters: Mining shutdowns signal stress in Bitcoin's hash-power base, while a large leverage overhang raises the odds of a sharp, mechanical price move in either direction.
whatToWatch: Whether rig shutdowns spread beyond the capital city
Price levels that could trigger forced liquidations across the leveraged position cluster
Any official explanation for why power to mining rigs was cut
questions: Which country's mining operations are affected, and why now?
How much of Bitcoin's global hashrate is at risk?

stories.title: Cboe pushes for 3x leveraged Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs despite steep losses in existing 2x funds
stories.summary: Cboe is advocating for 3x leveraged Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs even as existing 2x leveraged crypto funds have posted losses of up to 96%, according to CryptoSlate. The push comes even as current products illustrate how badly leverage decay can erode returns over time.
stories.whyItMatters: Higher-leverage crypto ETFs would let retail investors take on outsized, compounding risk right as current 2x products show how much value leverage decay can destroy.
whatToWatch: Whether regulators advance a 3x Bitcoin/Ethereum ETF filing
Performance trends in existing 2x leveraged crypto ETFs
Any added disclosure requirements regulators impose on leveraged crypto funds
questions: Which specific funds lost up to 96%, and over what timeframe?
Will regulators require stronger risk disclosures before approving 3x products?

sources.title: Cboe pushes for 3x Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs after 2x crypto funds suffer losses of up to 96%

stories.title: Ethereum and Solana look to shrink staking rewards just as Wall Street markets them as dividends
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that as Wall Street products increasingly market crypto staking yield to investors like a dividend, the Ethereum and Solana communities are weighing changes that would reduce staking rewards. The tension pits investment-product marketing against protocol-level moves to lower issuance.
stories.whyItMatters: A cut to staking rewards would directly affect the yield underpinning new staking-based investment products, changing the return profile investors were sold.
whatToWatch: Formal proposals to reduce Ethereum or Solana staking issuance
Reaction from asset managers marketing staking-yield products
Any timeline for implementing reward changes
questions: How much would rewards shrink, and on what schedule?
Have staking-yield product issuers responded publicly?

sources.title: Wall Street finally turned staking into a dividend, now Ethereum and Solana want to shrink it

stories.title: Solana-based reinsurance token sale relied on parent company Oxbridge for 95% of public demand
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that a Solana-based reinsurance token sale saw parent company Oxbridge account for roughly 95% of the public demand for tokens, raising questions about how organic the sale's investor interest actually was.
stories.whyItMatters: Heavy reliance on an affiliated buyer to fill a 'public' token sale is a red flag for real demand and price discovery in crypto capital raises.
whatToWatch: Whether Oxbridge discloses its stake or lock-up terms
Trading activity and price once the token lists
Any regulatory interest in insider-heavy token sales
questions: What portion of tokens is still held by Oxbridge after the sale?
Were retail buyers told about the concentration before investing?

stories.title: Nasdaq-listed Bitcoin treasury company diluted shareholders 18-fold to absorb a $212 million crypto loss
stories.summary: A Nasdaq-listed corporate Bitcoin treasury diluted its shareholders roughly 18-fold to cover a $212 million loss on its crypto holdings, rather than selling its Bitcoin stash, CryptoSlate reports.
stories.whyItMatters: It's a stark example of the balance-sheet risk behind corporate 'Bitcoin treasury' strategies — losses get absorbed by heavily diluting equity holders instead of touching the coins.
whatToWatch: The company's stock reaction and shareholder response
Whether other Bitcoin-treasury firms face similar dilution pressure
Any changes to the firm's treasury strategy going forward
questions: Which company is this, and how large is its total Bitcoin position?
Could further price declines force another dilution round?

stories.title: The SEC meeting that wasn't: crypto policy watchers left waiting
stories.summary: CoinDesk's State of Crypto column covers a widely anticipated SEC meeting on crypto policy that did not materialize as expected, leaving industry watchers without the clarity they had hoped for.
stories.whyItMatters: Regulatory clarity from the SEC remains one of the biggest swing factors for crypto market structure, and delays keep firms and investors in limbo.

Public statements from SEC commissioners on next steps

stories.title: The 'long bitcoin, short the bankers' trade is over as Wall Street embraces digital assets
stories.summary: CoinDesk reports that major traditional finance institutions are increasingly embracing digital assets directly, undercutting the once-popular crypto narrative of betting against banks by holding Bitcoin instead.
stories.whyItMatters: Deepening TradFi involvement changes crypto's ownership base and could soften the anti-institutional framing that helped drive early adoption.

Shifts in crypto ownership concentration between institutions and retail
Reaction from crypto-native investors to institutional entry
questions: Which institutions specifically are cited as embracing digital assets?

stories.title: Trump-linked World Liberty Financial gets OCC bank approval as its $112 million DeFi position nears liquidation
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that World Liberty Financial, the crypto venture linked to Trump, has won approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency for a bank charter, even as a $112 million DeFi position tied to the venture sits close to liquidation.
stories.whyItMatters: The approval marks a notable regulatory win for a politically connected crypto venture, while the at-risk DeFi position highlights financial exposure behind the scenes.
whatToWatch: Whether the $112 million position gets liquidated or is shored up
Next regulatory or operational steps following the OCC approval
Any political or ethics scrutiny of the approval
questions: What triggered the near-liquidation of the position?

stories.title: Crypto investors shift focus from market-cap rankings back to fundamentals
stories.summary: CoinDesk reports a shift in investor attention away from simple market-capitalization rankings toward underlying project fundamentals when evaluating crypto assets.
stories.whyItMatters: A fundamentals-first approach, if it holds, could reduce speculative rotation into tokens purely because they rank highly by market cap, changing how capital flows across the sector.
whatToWatch: Whether trading volumes and inflows start tracking fundamental metrics over rankings
Which projects benefit or lose out under this shift
questions: What specific fundamentals are investors prioritizing (revenue, usage, developer activity)?
Is this a durable trend or a short-term reaction to market conditions?

stories.title: MiCA's regulatory cleanup is fueling a new wave of crypto scams across the EU

stories.whyItMatters: MiCA was meant to make EU crypto markets safer; if its rollout is instead opening new scam vectors, it undercuts the framework's core investor-protection goal.

Enforcement actions from EU national regulators
Any MiCA amendments introduced to close loopholes
